account: It is day 1 at thirteen o'clock, and I have arrived at town hall for my council-letters appointment. The unusual business is the preparation of a large feast or gathering in the great hall without my yet knowing its purpose. Lanterns have been placed, and yesterday I personally saw builder and innkeeper deposit bread in a hall table chest. Neighbour identified builder as coordinator of supplies and lighting. Today baker said innkeeper had verified that all two hundred feast loaves arrived. Innkeeper has also told me local helpers are organising and that I need no prepared remarks. This suggests I may be expected at the gathering, but I do not know what it celebrates; a surprise celebration is a possibility, not an established fact. Secretary has been trying to establish the arrangements, but the last written report had no explanation from builder. There is also repeated talk among townsfolk of a bridge or port change at the bakery. I have seen no such change, and baker explicitly said it was only an unverified rumour. I should not treat that as official news or as evidence of the feast's purpose. My ten o'clock mill visit yielded no full grain-stock inspection; baker said miller handles those stocks. For now I intend to keep my council-letters appointment, ask secretary for any new information, and keep my fifteen-o'clock tea with Neighbour and sixteen-thirty office appointment.
